qualitative.filing_summary_10k: FOX's fiscal 2026 10-K reports total revenues of $17.1 billion, up 5% from fiscal 2025, driven by higher distribution, advertising and content revenues, with net income attributable to stockholders of $1,685 million, down from $2,263 million. The filing discloses FOX's June 2026 definitive merger agreement to acquire Roku for cash and stock, subject to stockholder and antitrust approvals, with termination fees ranging up to $1.2 billion. It also describes the August 2025 launch of the FOX One direct-to-consumer streaming service, $4.2 billion of cash on hand, approximately $2.3 billion returned to stockholders via dividends and buybacks (including a $1.5 billion accelerated share repurchase), and new debt commitments (Bridge and Term Loan Facilities) to help fund the Roku transaction.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: The Q3 fiscal 2026 10-Q (quarter ended March 31, 2026) shows revenues of $3,994 million for the quarter, down from $4,371 million a year earlier, and net income attributable to FOX stockholders of $166 million versus $346 million in the prior-year quarter; for the nine months, revenue was roughly flat at $12,914 million versus $13,013 million while net income attributable to stockholders fell to $994 million from $1,546 million. The filing reflects a large non-operating other, net loss of $499 million for the quarter, and reports weighted average diluted shares of 432 million versus 461 million a year earlier, consistent with share repurchase activity referenced elsewhere in the filings.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K, dated September 8, 2026, discloses that FOX and Roku each received a 'Second Request' for additional information from the U.S. Department of Justice as part of antitrust review of their previously announced merger agreement, which extends the HSR Act waiting period until 30 days after both companies substantially comply. The filing notes that FOX and Roku's joint proxy statement/prospectus was declared effective and mailed to stockholders around September 1, 2026, and that FOX expects the merger to close in the first half of calendar year 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and stockholder approvals.
qualitative.moat_explanation: The excerpts describe FOX's leadership positions and long track record in news (top-rated cable news for 24 years) and marquee live sports rights (NFL, MLB, World Series, Super Bowl, FIFA World Cup) secured under long-term contracts, along with brand strength in FOX News, FOX Sports, Tubi and FOX Entertainment that the company says supports affiliate fee and advertising price increases. These durable brand and content-rights advantages, rather than cost, network, switching-cost or scale-limitation dynamics, are what the excerpts most directly support.
red_flags: Pending Roku merger carries substantial termination fees (~$866 million mutual, up to ~$1.2 billion payable by FOX under certain conditions, plus up to $70 million reimbursement), and completion is uncertain pending antitrust/regulatory approval (DOJ issued a Second Request as of the 8-K).
Company explicitly acknowledges industry-wide decline in MVPD subscribers and negative impact on distribution/advertising revenue, expected to continue or accelerate.
Advertising revenue is described as volatile, cyclical (tied to sports events and elections) and pressured by ad-skipping/time-shifting technologies and increased competition from FAST/SVOD ad tiers.

Company is incurring significant new debt (Bridge Facility and Term Loan Facility, up to $12 billion in commitments) to fund the Roku merger, which the filing says could increase vulnerability to economic downturns and limit capital return capacity.
Uncertain impact of generative AI on content demand is noted as a risk with largely uncertain implications.
Merger Agreement restricts FOX's ability to pursue other acquisitions or issue equity without Roku's consent while the deal is pending.
